correctness.rationale: For 2<=p<=q, the assignment-to-incidence bijection requires distinct original tails and heads not among tails. For a tails-on-both-sides configuration, inclusion maximality is exactly surjectivity onto both unused original-side vertex sets, contributing (p-a)!S(b,p-a)(q-b)!S(a,q-b). All-one-side boundary configurations contribute q^p z^p and p^q z^q. The a+b spectrum from the surjection existence inequalities is {p} union {q,...,p+q-2}; largest induced size same upper bound. Independently brute-force adjacency subset enumeration agrees for six cases, including p=q=2 and p=2,q=5; arbitrary p,q follow the bijection and inequalities, not enumeration.
residual_risks: Finite brute force tests check only six small graphs; no claim for arbitrary partial subdivisions.
